evals.prompt: Make a one-page HTML capability statement for Big Sky Systems' Safety & Compliance service that I can send to a prospect. Include a short intro, what's included, a small table of the standards we work against (ISO 10218, ISO/TS 15066, ANSI/RIA R15.06), a typical timeline, and a call to action to email build@bigsky.systems. Single self-contained HTML file named safety-one-pager.html.
evals.expected_output: A single HTML file on bone paper with the dot grid, Archivo headings, one serif italic accent word, mono uppercase eyebrows numbered 01 //, a spec table with hairline rows and an ink header underline, an ink primary button with an arrow, corner marks on panels, orange used only for numbers/dash/one word. No gradients, pills, or shadows.
assertions: design language checks (fonts, paper bg, orange accent, no SaaS palette, no gradients, radii <= 4px, no shadows, mono uppercase labels, numbered labels, no emoji)
all three standards named inside a <table>

evals.prompt: Build a small self-contained HTML dashboard page called cell-uptime.html for Big Sky Systems showing last week's uptime for four robot cells (Cell A 97.2%, Cell B 91.5%, Cell C 99.1%, Cell D 84.3%): a bar chart, a stat row with the fleet average and the worst cell, and a short list of the top three faults (gripper timeout 14, vision retry 9, e-stop 2). No external JS libraries.
evals.expected_output: A paper-sheet dashboard: mono uppercase axis labels, hairline gridlines, ink bars with the worst cell highlighted in orange, stat rows (mono label left, Archivo number right) instead of colored KPI cards, a square-marker fault list, a FIG. caption. Fleet average 93.0%, worst cell D.
